primary_task: Fix a reported bug in a repository by first writing a failing reproduction test, then implementing the fix and running the repository's full test suite.

requirements.name: repository test runner (npm test, ./gradlew test, pytest, go test, ...)
requirements.evidence: Run the repository's focused-test command during the loop and its full-suite command before completion.
requirements.basis: tools.bash: "install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads), build, test, run CLIs and scripts"

requirements.name: read/write/edit
requirements.evidence: Write a failing test before writing the code that makes it pass.
requirements.basis: tools.write: "create and overwrite files"; tools.edit: "edit existing files and Jupyter notebooks"

requirements.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
requirements.evidence: For browser-based changes, combine TDD with runtime verification using Chrome DevTools MCP
requirements.basis: lacks: "connectors or integrations other than the tools listed"

requirements.name: sub-agents
requirements.evidence: For complex bug fixes, spawn a subagent to write the reproduction test
requirements.basis: tools.agent: "start sub-agents that work in parallel, send them messages and list them"

notes: The test runner depends on the repository's stack; most (pytest, npm, go, Gradle via wrapper) are obtainable from open registries, but a stack whose tooling or dependencies live on refused hosts would be unknown (for example a Gradle wrapper downloading from services.gradle.org, which the manifest does not list). Chrome DevTools MCP applies only to browser-based changes; for a browser-based request the reading that makes it hard would give BLOCKED on connector:Chrome DevTools MCP.
